content.text:
I changed `totalPaidCents` in `src/services/order-service.js` so the paid-total report leaves out orders from soft-deleted users. It still uses callbacks. I didn't run the tests, as you asked.

It now does two queries, one inside the other:
1. It gets the users whose `deleted_at` is `null` and collects their IDs.
2. It gets the orders that are paid, not deleted, and belong to one of those users, then adds up `total_cents` as before.

With the seed data, order 13 (Alan, soft-deleted) drops out, so the total goes from 14600 to 14100. Any test that expects the old number will need updating.

`src/repositories/order-repository.js` has a matching paid-total query (line 13) that still counts soft-deleted users' orders. I left it alone because you only asked for the service. If the Chapter 5 migration moves callers over to the repository, it will need the same change or the reports will disagree.

content.text:
I updated the failing test in `tests/order-service.test.js` to expect 14100 instead of 14600, and renamed it to "counts only paid orders from active users". It was failing because it still counted order 13, which belongs to soft-deleted user Alan, and leaving that order out is what you asked for. I haven't run the tests myself, since you asked me not to, so the stop hook's next run is the first check of this fix.

The hook output also showed a second, odd assertion with `actual: AssertionError` and `expected: null`. That comes from `query` in `src/db.js`: it calls your callback inside a `try`, so when an assertion in the test callback throws, `query` calls the same callback a second time with that error. It only shows up when a test is already failing. I didn't touch it.
